title: CI matrix omits Windows (and macOS) although the plugin ships Windows-specific hook commands and fcntl-less code paths
scenario: hooks/hooks.json ships `commandWindows: py -3 ...` for every hook (lines 10, 21, 34) and the kernel has dedicated no-fcntl fallbacks (loop.py:203, kb.py:76), yet the only runner is ubuntu-latest with python 3.10-3.12 (ci.yml:12-16). A regression in Windows path normalization (norm() vs backslashes), the `py -3` launcher, or the ImportError lock fallback ships completely untested; the first signal is a user's locked workspace on a host CI never exercised. 477 tests exist — they just never run where half the hook config points.
fix: Add `windows-latest` (and ideally `macos-latest`) to the tests job matrix; mark the few POSIX-only tests with skipif rather than skipping the platform.

title: Build inputs pinned only by mutable tag: actions @v4/@v5 and an unversioned `pip install pytest`
scenario: actions/checkout@v4 (line 18) and actions/setup-python@v5 (line 20) are floating tags a compromised or breaking release can move; `pip install pytest` (line 25) takes whatever major pytest ships next. The same jobs validate the release package (package_openai.py runs here, line 63), so a moved tag is inside the release-trust path. A pytest 9 behavior change can also flip CI red/green with zero repo change, breaking the reproducibility the project's own DevOps lens charter demands.
fix: Pin actions to full commit SHAs (with the tag as a comment) and pytest to a version range (`pip install "pytest==8.*"`); Dependabot can keep the SHAs fresh.

title: No `permissions:` block — jobs run with the default GITHUB_TOKEN scope though both only read contents
scenario: Neither the tests job nor validate-plugin needs anything beyond contents: read, but with no permissions block the workflow inherits the repository default, which on many repos is read-write. Combined with the unpinned third-party actions above, a malicious action update would hold a token able to push. Least-privilege here is a two-line change.
fix: Add top-level `permissions: { contents: read }` to ci.yml.

title: CI rebuilds the OpenAI zip but never compares it to the committed dist/ artifact — released-artifact drift is undetected
scenario: The packager is fully deterministic (fixed zip timestamps, sorted members, fixed modes — verified: a fresh rebuild at c8b6c9f reproduces sha256 da40a274bad84d991175cdfd0754f16cf46f113b3b373303f435d9b3d4d020b5, byte-identical to dist/taskplane-2.2.1-openai.zip.sha256), yet CI writes its build to dist/ on a checkout and asserts nothing about the committed zip. A skills edit merged without re-running scripts/package_openai.py leaves a stale dist/ artifact that users/marketplace download, with green CI.
fix: In validate-plugin, build to a temp dir and `cmp` the fresh zip's sha256 against dist/*.sha256, failing on mismatch — determinism makes this a one-line gate.

title: PRIVACY.md claims kb lint 'mechanically blocks' sensitive content from the store, but lint gates nothing at write or publish time
scenario: PRIVACY.md:31 tells the user the committed knowledge store is 'decision data only — the `kb lint` check mechanically blocks prompt text, raw model content, and pricing/commercial strategy from the store.' In reality `kb.lint` is only invoked at the DoD exit gate (tp.py:710) and the EM gate (loop.py:1730). It is NOT called by `kb.record_decision` (kb.py:104, which writes the ADR + index directly) nor by `kb.publish`/`tp share push` (kb.py:206, which copies decisions into the committed `.taskplane-kb/` shared store). So on a team/enterprise plan a user can `tp req`/record decisions containing prompt text, raw model output, PII, or pricing strategy, and `tp share push` will publish them into the git-committed, team-visible (potentially public) store WITHOUT lint ever running — the policy's central mechanical guarantee does not exist on the path where it matters most. It is also substring-marker matching only, which cannot actually detect 'raw model content' or personal data.
fix: Run `kb.lint` (at minimum the PROMPT_MARKERS/SENSITIVE_MARKERS scan) inside `kb.publish._publish_locked` before copying each entry to the shared store, and reject/skip flagged entries; ideally also lint at `record_decision` write time. If enforcement is intentionally gate-only, correct PRIVACY.md to say lint 'flags such content at the DoD/EM gate' rather than 'mechanically blocks it from the store', so the policy statement matches actual behavior.

title: Compose-them promise overclaims: review findings do NOT land in the knowledge base
scenario: README's 'Compose them -> review, then fix' section states '(findings land in the knowledge base)' and 'The review's findings become the fix loop's input'. In code, a standalone tp-engineering review writes only .em-review/findings.json, which `tp init` explicitly adds to .gitignore (tp.py:1241); no code path in kb.py, tp.py, or loop.py records .em-review content into the KB (grep for 'em-review' in kb.py: zero hits; _publish_artifacts fires only on loop gates). On Claude Tag — whose sandbox is ephemeral and whose persistence story is exactly 'the KB travels with the branch' (README line 465) — a review followed by 'tp-go: fix the blockers' in the next session finds no findings at all: the git-ignored file died with the sandbox.
fix: Smallest fix: have the tp-engineering skill end a review by recording a findings digest into the KB (`tp kb record` or per-blocker `tp req debt` entries), which also makes the claim true on Tag; or soften the README sentence to 'findings persist in .em-review/ in your working copy'.

title: No issue/PR templates or CONTRIBUTING guide, though SUPPORT.md routes everyone to GitHub issues with a required-info list
scenario: .github/ contains only workflows/ci.yml — no ISSUE_TEMPLATE, no PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE, no CONTRIBUTING.md anywhere in the repo. SUPPORT.md (line 4) directs all defect/feature traffic to GitHub issues and then enumerates what a report must include (taskplane version, host + host version, OS, command/workflow, minimal repro) — a list the reporter only sees if they happen to read SUPPORT.md first. Result: unstructured issues missing the triage fields the maintainer already specified, and a new contributor has no documented way to even run the test suite (pytest invocation is discoverable only inside ci.yml).
fix: Add .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml encoding SUPPORT.md's field list (plus a feature-request form), and a minimal CONTRIBUTING.md: clone, `cd taskplane && python -m pytest tests/ -q`, style expectations, and the release/regeneration steps.

title: Three conflicting severity vocabularies across lens prompts, the tp-lens agent, and the EM gate
scenario: lenses/*.md mandate the shared verdict format with severity 'blocker|major|minor|question|praise' (e.g. lenses/tech-writer.md:50); agents/tp-lens.md:54 mandates 'high|med|low'; and the EM gate treats only 'critical'/'high' as blocking (taskplane/loop.py:1258-1265). An EM that faithfully copies a lens's 'blocker' finding into .em-review/findings.json passes `loop gate` with that blocker unresolved, because 'blocker' is not in the gate's severity set.
fix: Pick one severity taxonomy (or publish an explicit mapping) and apply it consistently in lenses/*.md, agents/tp-lens.md, and _engineering_review_errors — at minimum make the gate treat 'blocker' as blocking.

title: HUMAN row omits the A/B `selection` gate the engine enforces
scenario: A reader auditing decision authority before enabling A/B builds reads 'the loop pauses at design_approval, plan_approval, signoff, escalated; nothing advances these steps but an explicit human command' and concludes variant selection is agent-decidable. The shipped engine adds `selection` to HUMAN_STEPS (taskplane/loop.py:75-77), parks the loop there, refuses `loop approve` for it (loop.py:1929-1931), and requires an explicit human `loop select`.
fix: Add `selection` (A/B pick of what ships) to the HUMAN row's 'May decide' list and to the pause list, and add the selection gate to the Escalation paths section.

title: Attribution rules absent: design approval hard-requires --by; anonymous plan/signoff approvals are recorded '(unattributed)'
scenario: A team writes its gate-audit policy from the matrix's Audit section, which lists 'human sign-offs' as traced but says nothing about attribution. In v2.2.1, `loop approve` at design_approval errors without --by, while plan_approval/signoff accept an anonymous approve, substitute by='(unattributed)', emit only a warning, and trace loop_approve_unattributed (taskplane/loop.py:1845-1857). An auditor expecting uniformly attributed gate passes finds unattributed entries the doc never mentioned.
fix: Document the per-gate attribution asymmetry in the HUMAN row and the Audit section: design approval requires --by; plan approval and sign-off record '(unattributed)' with a warning when --by is omitted.

title: PM row's DoD overstates what the shipped (v2.2.1 fail-closed) pm gate enforces
scenario: The doc frames the loop as 'mechanically gated, not honor-system' (line 40) and its per-step table gives PM the DoD 'testable acceptance criteria + requirement dependencies/contracts'. The shipped pm gate (taskplane/loop.py:1474-1498, the v2.2.1 H4 fix) mechanically enforces only 'a non-empty specs/spec.md exists OR a requirement_id is attached' — a one-line untestable spec passes the gate. A reader relying on the table believes criteria quality is machine-checked at pm.
fix: Update the PM row (and the state-machine diagram's PM DoD annotation) to state the actual minimal fail-closed check, noting that testable-criteria quality is the role's obligation validated later by the refinement gate, not the pm gate.

title: The submission worksheet is stale at 2.2.0 while the release is 2.2.1 — its checklist points at an artifact the build can no longer produce
scenario: The worksheet's build section (lines 50-51) and portal checklist (line 178) instruct uploading `dist/taskplane-2.2.0-openai.zip`, but scripts/package_openai.py names the archive from the manifest version (package_openai.py:365), which is 2.2.1 — the local dist/ actually holds taskplane-2.2.1-openai.zip. The 'Submission release notes' (line 153) describe 2.2.0, omitting every 2.2.1 fix, and line 182 says to confirm URLs 'after the 2.2.0 changes are pushed'. A person executing this runbook today either stalls hunting for a nonexistent file or submits release notes for the wrong version.
fix: Re-stamp the worksheet to 2.2.1 (title, artifact names, release notes, checklist) as part of the release procedure, and — per the time-to-market lens — parameterize the artifact name ('dist/taskplane-<manifest version>-openai.zip') so the doc stops embedding a hardcoded version.

title: Shipped security-lens reference escalates to machinery that does not exist in taskplane (Conductor, the Board, a CSO)
scenario: Lines 207-208 of the security lens's deep-audit reference instruct: PASS-WITH-CONDITIONS -> 'Conductor schedules follow-up'; FAIL -> 'return to loop-execution-evaluator -> Conductor dispatches loop-fixer; CRITICAL/HIGH ... convene the Board (CSO leading)'. taskplane ships no Conductor, no Board, no CSO, and its evaluator/fixer agents are named tp-evaluator/tp-fixer — the project even explicitly disavows executive simulation (tp-northstar: 'no executive cosplay'). A security tp-lens subagent dutifully following its own reference at the verdict step tries to invoke undefined roles, producing confusion or hallucinated escalation in the findings it returns.
fix: Rewrite the escalation table in taskplane terms: PASS-WITH-CONDITIONS -> record conditions as findings + `tp req debt`; FAIL (critical/high) -> blocker findings that fail the evaluate gate and route to tp-fixer via the loop's existing fix cycle.

title: 'No unexplained drift' wording contradicts the shipped gate, which blocks ANY recorded drift
scenario: README.md:56, the CHANGELOG v2.2.0 row, and this skill ('no unexplained drift') tell a reviewer that explained drift can coexist with sign-off. The gate fails on any non-empty meta.design.drift list (taskplane/design_contract.py:503-504) — a reviewer who dutifully records an explained, accepted deviation is blocked, while skills/tp-design/references/design-contract.md:145 correctly says 'Any drift blocks sign-off'. The doc surfaces disagree with each other and with the engine.
fix: Align README, CHANGELOG, and SKILL wording with the mechanism: any recorded drift blocks sign-off and routes back through Design; drop the 'unexplained' qualifier (or implement an accepted-drift path first).

title: The enforcement-core README speaks a pre-rename vocabulary ('Conductor roles', 'engineering-manager role') and misstates the plugin license as MIT
scenario: A new contributor opening taskplane/README.md — the doc for the very core they'd modify — reads at line 3 that this is 'the enforcement core for Conductor roles' (the ancestor project's name, appearing nowhere else in shipped docs), later an 'engineering-manager role' that shipped as tp-engineering, and at line 79 'Apache-2.0 (taskplane); bundled inside the MIT-licensed plugin' — while LICENSE, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, and .codex-plugin/plugin.json all say Apache-2.0 and no MIT license exists in the repo. The contributor is left unsure which role names are real and which license governs their contribution.
fix: One sweep of taskplane/README.md: replace 'Conductor roles' with 'taskplane roles (tp-*)', 'engineering-manager' with 'tp-engineering', and correct line 79 to state the whole plugin is Apache-2.0.

title: Generated lens catalog is not checked for drift against its markdown sources
scenario: lenses/catalog.json drives all routing/dispatch, and generators exist to derive artifacts from the lens sources (scripts/gen_lens_catalog.py, lenses/_generate_catalog.py, lenses/_generate_lens_prompts.py), but CI never regenerates and diffs. Editing lenses/backend.md's checks without re-running the generator leaves the router dispatching stale checks — silently, since manifest validation only parses JSON. Evidence such drift already happens: lens.py:_HARD_LENSES names a 'concurrency' lens absent from the 26-entry catalog.
fix: Add a CI step: run the catalog/prompt generators and `git diff --exit-code lenses/` so generated artifacts provably match their sources.

title: README/CHANGELOG cross-references disagree, leaving v2.1.0 unreachable from the README
scenario: CHANGELOG.md:3 says 'The two most recent releases are summarized in the README', but README's table holds three (2.2.1, 2.2.0, 2.0.0) — and skips v2.1.0 entirely. README.md:59's pointer covers only 'Older releases (v1.0.0 – v1.6.0)', so v2.1.0 — a real feature release (evidence/fingerprint gating) — is invisible to anyone navigating from the README: not in the table, not in the pointer's stated range.
fix: Change README.md:59 to 'All earlier releases: see CHANGELOG.md', fix CHANGELOG.md:3 to match the actual policy (or adopt 'latest N releases' wording), and either add the v2.1.0 row or accept the pointer as the single path to it.

title: 'A worker cannot advance its own stage' is stated as mechanical; the engine documents it as a protocol guarantee
scenario: README says a worker 'cannot advance its own stage. The orchestrator independently runs the engine gate', and the bullet at line 369 says 'only the orchestrator invokes the state-transition gate'. loop.py:1273-1279 (the v2.2.1 L12 note) states this is a PROTOCOL guarantee: any process with workspace access can call gate(); what holds mechanically is the evidence fingerprint. The 'Honest about what the guardrails are' section covers the hook but not this nuance, so a reader assumes caller identity is enforced.
fix: Add one sentence to the honest-limits section mirroring the L12 note: orchestrator-only gating is protocol + trace attribution; the mechanical guarantee is that a gate only advances on fingerprint-matching evidence.

title: Release notes are hand-maintained in two places (README 'What's new' table + CHANGELOG) and have already diverged
scenario: Every release writes the same prose twice: a row in README's 'What's new' (line 53) and a row in CHANGELOG.md. The two copies already disagree structurally — CHANGELOG.md:3 promises 'the two most recent releases' appear in the README while the README table carries three (2.2.1, 2.2.0, 2.0.0) — and the v2.2.1 texts differ between files, so a reader can't tell which is canonical. Double authoring on the release critical path, drift as the steady state.
fix: Follow the repo's own generator pattern (scripts/gen_lens_catalog.py): derive the README rows from the top N CHANGELOG entries via a small script run at release, or replace the table with a two-line summary plus a link to CHANGELOG.md.

title: TECHNICAL row says lenses' write-allow is '.eval/** only'; lens subagents write .em-review/lens-<id>/**
scenario: A reader verifying the enforcement claims checks a tp-lens agent's contract during an EM review and finds write-allow '.em-review/lens-<id>/**' (agents/tp-lens.md:29,53), not '.eval/**' — the matrix's 'Enforced by' cell for 'lenses & the evaluator' describes only the evaluator's contract.
fix: State both write-allows in the row: evaluator → .eval/**, lens subagents → .em-review/lens-<id>/**.

title: Generated lens-catalog doc has no CI freshness check — regeneration is a manual step that can be silently skipped
scenario: docs/lens-catalog.md:5 declares itself GENERATED from lenses/catalog.json by scripts/gen_lens_catalog.py ('regenerate — don't hand-edit'), but no ci.yml step regenerates and diffs it. Add or amend a lens without rerunning the script and the shipped catalog doc silently disagrees with the machine catalog — the exact drift class v1.5.4's notes say kept happening — discovered only when a user counts lenses.
fix: Add one CI step: run `python3 scripts/gen_lens_catalog.py` and `git diff --exit-code docs/lens-catalog.md`, failing the build when the doc is stale (same pattern as the existing manifest-agreement check).

title: Historical draft shipped without a status banner; superseded details read as current
scenario: Unlike loop-design.md (which opens 'Status: SHIPPED' and explains how to read it), this doc still opens 'Draft for your input' and describes subagent lenses writing to '.review/<lens>/' (line 196) and an in-repo 'knowledge/' layout (line 110) — both superseded (.em-review/lens-<id>/ and the plan-aware store). Only decision 3 carries a supersession note; a reader takes the rest as shipped behavior.
fix: Add a status header matching loop-design.md's pattern (design record; superseded paths noted) and correct or annotate the .review/<lens>/ and knowledge/ references.

title: Submission worksheet still pinned to 2.2.0 in the 2.2.1 release
scenario: The doc is titled 'taskplane 2.2.0' and instructs uploading dist/taskplane-2.2.0-openai.zip, but the release ships dist/taskplane-2.2.1-openai.zip — a maintainer following the worksheet verbatim looks for an artifact name the packager no longer produces.
fix: Bump the versioned title and artifact names as part of the release checklist (or make them version-neutral: 'dist/taskplane-<version>-openai.zip').

title: The env-var surface (9+ variables) is scattered and mostly undocumented — integrators discover knobs by reading source
scenario: Behavior-changing environment variables span TASKPLANE_HOME, TASKPLANE_STORE, TASKPLANE_ORPHAN_TTL, TASKPLANE_AGENT_PID, TASKPLANE_MODEL_CHEAP/_STANDARD/_DEEP, TASKPLANE_ENFORCE_DISPATCH, plus the host probes CODEX_HOME/CODEX_THREAD_ID and the hook roots PLUGIN_ROOT/CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT. state-spec.md documents only TASKPLANE_STORE and TASKPLANE_HOME; ORPHAN_TTL, AGENT_PID and ENFORCE_DISPATCH exist only in code comments/help strings. An embedder wiring taskplane into another harness (e.g. a CI sandbox needing a longer orphan TTL, or wanting strict dispatch enforcement) has no reference page and no way to see which values are in effect — a wrong TASKPLANE_STORE silently redirects the whole knowledge store.
fix: Add an 'Environment variables' table to docs/state-spec.md (name, default, consumer, effect) and surface the RESOLVED values in one introspection point — extend `tp onboard --json` (which already reports model_tiers) with store/orphan_ttl/enforce_dispatch/host.

title: loop.json field description is stale for v2.2.1: `_submission` blocks unlisted, 'captured on entry to Design' no longer accurate
scenario: Someone auditing what a repo-committed loop.json contains in Claude Tag mode (TASKPLANE_STORE=repo) reads the 'Design state and evidence' section and expects design flags plus fingerprints. The shipped file also persists worker `_submission` evidence blocks — absolute workspace paths, changed-file lists, fingerprints (taskplane/loop.py:1330-1365) — and since v2.2.1 (H3) the design graph baseline re-captures on every pre-approval rescan (loop.py:631-645), not once 'on entry to Design'.
fix: Refresh the section: enumerate the v2.2.1 loop.json keys including `_submission`, and describe the pre-approval rebaseline behavior.

title: Dead code: catalog loaded three times, first result immediately discarded
scenario: Lines 29-30 compute `lenses` by opening and json.load-ing catalog.json three times in one expression; lines 32-33 then re-read the file and overwrite `lenses`, with a comment admitting the first statement is vestigial. The dead statement still executes (3 extra parses, 4 unclosed file handles including line 106's open(OUT,'w').write) and misleads a reader into thinking the double-read is load-bearing.
fix: Delete lines 29-31, keep the clean read at 32-33, and use `with open(...)` for both the read and the final write.

title: Claims Design DoR requires an 'explicit boundary policy'; the engine checks that at DoD
scenario: The skill says 'Design DoR requires a refined requirement, current baseline graph, explicit boundary policy, and no blocking questions'. design_dor() (taskplane/design_contract.py:104-132) checks requirement/acceptance/open-questions/graph baseline/current-state only; depth_policy and boundary_mode are validated by design_dod_errors. A driver checking the boundary policy before letting Design start is checking something the entry gate never evaluates.
fix: Move 'explicit boundary policy' from the DoR sentence to the DoD sentence in this skill.
